title: Multi-command batch can drive the budget negative: apply_all validates each cmd against the un-mutated budget and spend() has no floor
detail: Phase 1 checks each DrawPipe against the original budget, so two draws each <= budget both pass; Phase 2 spends both, pushing budget below 0. spend() never floors. ACR-E23 permits multi-cmd batches.
recommended_fix: Validate each command against the progressively-mutated state (track a running batch cost, or re-validate after each apply), or floor budget at 0 in spend().

title: apply_* deref entities via direct _pipes[]/_nodes[] with no null guard; a batch can target a just-removed entity
detail: A batch [Demolish pipe P, SetLaneWeights P] validates ok (both see P in the un-mutated graph), then apply removes P and the next apply reads _pipes[P] with no guard -> null access on the now-absent entity.
recommended_fix: Guard each apply read (early-return if absent) or re-validate each command against the progressively-mutated graph inside apply_all's apply phase.

title: ScriptedDirector._load uses the FileAccess.open() result with no null check; the parallel catalogs._read_json does guard it
detail: file_exists can pass yet open() return null (permissions, export packed-data edge). f.get_as_text() then derefs null instead of setting load_ok=false. The sibling loader guards exactly this; the director does not.
recommended_fix: Add `if f == null: push_error(...); load_ok = false; return` right after open, mirroring catalogs._read_json.

title: NetworkHealth.update derefs balance unconditionally though _init tolerates a null balance
detail: _init's null-guard implies balance may be null, but update() reads balance.win_uptime_pct / meter_drain_per_tick_max / meter_recharge_per_tick unguarded -> null deref if constructed without balance. PacketFlow guards balance everywhere; this one does not.
recommended_fix: Drop the null default in _init (require balance) or guard balance in update() like PacketFlow does (fall back to compile-time constants).
